themes_detail.label: Encampment surge in parks
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked to 18 this week versus a 3.1-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—a 476% increase (z-score: 3.83)—coinciding with a simultaneous 367% spike in park rules violations (7 complaints this week vs. 1.5 weekly average), suggesting a rapid destabilization of park safety and usage this week.
evidence: 18 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.1-per-week average over prior 8 weeks (476% spike, z-score 3.83)
7 park rules violations THIS WEEK vs. 1.5-per-week average (367% spike, z-score 4.92)
Community board has repeatedly requested enhanced park safety through more security staff and police/parks enforcement
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept and NYPD about what triggered the sudden uptick in encampments and rule violations this week
Talk to park users and nearby residents about perceived safety changes in specific parks (Inwood Hill, Fort Tryon, etc.)
Investigate whether the encampment surge correlates with recent shelter placements, weather, or enforcement changes

themes_detail.label: Abandoned bikes proliferating
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints exploded to 3 this week—a 700% surge above the 0.4-per-week baseline (z-score: 5.42)—suggesting a new or accelerating problem with bike clutter and theft in the district this week.
evidence: 3 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4-per-week average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Spike is extremely recent, appearing only this week with no prior escalation signal
reporting_angles: Survey visible bike abandonment in high-traffic areas (subway stations, commercial strips) to assess street-level reality
Interview NYC Department of Transportation about abandoned bike removal protocols and response times
Speak with bike shop owners and residents about theft trends and whether stolen bikes are being dumped

themes_detail.label: For-hire vehicle complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 18 two weeks ago—a 1100% surge above the 1.5-per-week baseline (z-score: 19.05, highest severity)—suggesting a possible crackdown, surge in Uber/Lyft activity, or parking/congestion problem tied to ride-sharing in the district.
evidence: 18 for-hire vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.5-per-week baseline (1100% spike, z-score 19.05, highest z-score in dataset)
This is the single largest statistical anomaly in the recent 311 data, suggesting a discrete event or policy change
Broader parking complaints remain chronically high (2,722 over 90 days), suggesting structural congestion
reporting_angles: Determine if NYPD or TLC launched an enforcement operation against for-hire vehicles in Washington Heights/Inwood two weeks ago
Interview residents and local businesses about the impact of for-hire vehicle congestion on street parking and traffic
Check if ride-share companies expanded service, changed driver incentives, or launched a surge-pricing event in that timeframe

themes_detail.label: Water system failures escalating
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints surged to 41 two weeks ago—a 215% increase above the 13-per-week baseline (z-score: 7.84)—indicating a potential citywide or district-specific water main or infrastructure issue that warrants urgent investigation.
evidence: 41 water system complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 13-per-week baseline (215% spike, z-score 7.84)
Heat/hot water complaints remain the highest-volume complaint category overall (5,936 over 90 days), suggesting chronic winter heating challenges
Water leaks (640 complaints over 90 days) and plumbing complaints (1,079) indicate broader water infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection about water main breaks, pressure issues, or water quality alerts in Washington Heights/Inwood two weeks ago
Interview building superintendents and residents about whether water outages or low-pressure events occurred around the spike date
Investigate whether aging infrastructure in upper Manhattan is vulnerable to seasonal failure or whether a specific incident triggered the spike

themes_detail.label: Mobile food vendor complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints surged to 3 last week—a 2300% increase above the 0.1-per-week baseline (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting either a new enforcement focus, an influx of unlicensed vendors, or rapid expansion of street food activity in the district.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints last week vs. 0.1-per-week baseline (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Extremely rare baseline (nearly zero complaints historically) makes even small absolute numbers statistically extreme
Spike is very recent (last week), suggesting a sudden change in vendor activity or enforcement
reporting_angles: Survey street-level food vendor presence in commercial districts (168th St, Broadway) to assess density and licensing
Interview Department of Health and Mental Hygiene about whether a crackdown on unlicensed vendors began recently
Talk to residents and business owners about whether street food vendor presence and sanitation practices have changed noticeably
